steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A sacrament is an outward sign of an inward grace — a visible ceremony that Christians believe channels God's grace (favour) to the believer. Most Christians recognise two sacraments (Baptism and Eucharist) but Catholics and Orthodox recognise seven.

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: The Eucharist is the most important act of worship for Catholics — they believe they receive Christ himself. For Protestants, it is a memorial that strengthens faith and unity. Be ready to explain both views with specific theological terms.

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — Sacraments: Baptism and Eucharist
steps.body: 1. For Sacraments: Baptism and Eucharist questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of Sacraments: Baptism and Eucharist to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
